decisions.reason: As a newly launched product with its own page and very close fit to the firm's integrated airport operations offer, it is likely to be retained while management learns from early market feedback in a growing business with slack and R&D capacity.

Because this module builds directly on the firm's established apron and integration capabilities, boundedly rational management would likely keep it for another year unless clear evidence of underperformance emerges.

Although somewhat less central to the firm's core operational-control positioning than other launches, it still extends the software stack for airport customers and is likely to be given more time before being judged against aspirations.

This product fits the firm's move toward data-driven monitoring and lifecycle service integration, so management would likely continue it while exploiting complementarities with installed equipment and service relationships.
Given its close relation to the firm's existing apron coordination offer and the firm's current expansion and investment, management would likely retain it despite normal early-stage uncertainty.

A safety-oriented service is strongly aligned with the firm's value proposition to airports and air navigation providers, making retention likely unless performance falls well below aspiration levels.
